answer: Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 347 answers need 347 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Because the ripple index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the ember audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the ridge identifier and voids the later submissions, so that the operator burns for 347 runs and collects one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
